action: Enforce dust mitigation: store and cover C&D materials and waste, move them only in covered vehicles, use anti-smog guns and water sprinkling.
C&D projects of 500 sq m or more that are not registered on the State/GNCTD dust-monitoring web portal are not permitted to carry out C&D activities.
Diesel generator sets must not be used as a regular power source; their use is regulated under CAQM Direction No. 76.
Intensified inspections to enforce dust-control measures at C&D sites.

Strict restrictions across NCR on dust-generating work: excavation, boring and drilling, piling, demolition, open-trench cabling and pipe laying, brick/masonry work, RMC batching plants, major welding and gas cutting, painting and plastering, tile and stone cutting, road construction and major repairs (pothole repair allowed), loading/unloading of dust-generating materials, and construction vehicles on unpaved roads.

Less dust-generating work may continue with strict dust-control compliance. Railway, metro, airport/ISBT, defence/national-importance, hospital, linear public and sanitation/water-supply projects may continue all activities.
Stone crushers and all mining activities closed across NCR.
The Stage III restrictions also apply to linear public projects such as highways, roads, flyovers, power transmission, pipelines and telecommunication.
Strict PUC enforcement; visibly polluting vehicles impounded or fined; ban on overaged diesel/petrol vehicles enforced.
Trucks not bound for Delhi diverted through the Eastern and Western Peripheral Expressways.
Only EV, CNG or BS-VI diesel inter-city/inter-state buses may ply in Delhi-NCR.
Vehicle parking fees increased to discourage private transport.
Diesel BS-IV and older light and medium goods vehicles registered outside Delhi are not allowed to enter Delhi; Delhi-registered diesel BS-IV and older medium goods vehicles are restricted in Delhi.
BS-III petrol and BS-IV diesel four-wheelers restricted in Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Sonipat, Ghaziabad and Gautam Buddha Nagar.
Truck (HGV) entry into Delhi stopped and Delhi-registered diesel BS-IV and older HGVs banned; LNG, CNG, electric and BS-VI diesel trucks are allowed.
States may consider emergency measures such as closing non-emergency commercial activities and odd-even vehicle rules.

Classes up to Class V in hybrid mode (physical and online where feasible) in Delhi, Gurugram, Faridabad, Ghaziabad and Gautam Buddha Nagar; other NCR areas may follow. The online option rests with students and guardians.
Classes VI to IX and XI also move to hybrid mode in the same areas.
States may consider closing colleges and educational institutions.
Court orders on firecrackers strictly enforced.
No coal or firewood in tandoors at hotels, restaurants and open eateries; only electric, gas or clean-fuel appliances.
Diesel generator sets must not be used as a regular power source; their use is regulated under CAQM Direction No. 76.
Citizen charter: avoid outdoor smoke-generating cooking and heating, and use public transport.
Citizen charter: postpone private gatherings that increase traffic and outdoor exposure.
Citizens advised to limit non-essential outdoor activity; children, the elderly and people with heart or lung conditions should stay indoors.
